rules.definition: A classical planet receives another when the guest occupies one of the host planet's domiciles and host and guest are configured by a recognized sign-based aspect.
rules.source_reference: Christopher Brennan, Hellenistic Astrology (2017), glossary: reception; ch. 14, Mitigating Conditions: Reception, pp. 491–494.

rules.definition: Two classical planets exchange domiciles when each occupies a domicile of the other.
rules.source_reference: Christopher Brennan, Hellenistic Astrology (2017), glossary: exchange.

rules.definition: Compatibility label for an exchange pair that also has reciprocal domicile reception through a recognized configuration. It is kept separate from the Hellenistic exchange relation and is not used to rewrite it.
rules.source_reference: Christopher Brennan, Hellenistic Astrology (2017), glossary: mutual reception and exchange.
rules.tradition_note: Later-tradition compatibility label; distinct identifier retained so Hellenistic exchange and later mutual-reception terminology are never silently collapsed.

rules.definition: For sign-based sextile, square, or trine configurations, the planet on the right/earlier side of the zodiacal configuration is in the superior position and overcomes the planet on the left/later side.
rules.source_reference: Christopher Brennan, Hellenistic Astrology (2017), glossary: overcoming/right; ch. 14, Overcoming, pp. 466–470.

rules.definition: A square in which the superior planet is in the tenth sign relative to the inferior planet is the especially forceful form of overcoming called domination/upon-the-tenth.
rules.source_reference: Christopher Brennan, Hellenistic Astrology (2017), glossary: domination; ch. 14, Overcoming, pp. 466–470.

epistemic_boundary: These are astrological rule models. They do not establish physical causation or empirical efficacy.
